pick.headline: Kohl and Gorbachev agree a united Germany may join NATO
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of July 19, 1990, carried a report of Shevardnadze's Paris talks with Baker, Genscher and Meckel on carrying out the Gorbachev-Kohl accords, with Shevardnadze saying no foreign troops or nuclear weapons would be placed on former East German territory.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Soviet Union, No. 139, 19 July 1990
evidence.snippet: …jects covered by Soviet-U.S. dialogue. The Shevardnadze-Genscher meeting dealt with specific approaches to the fulfilment of recent accords reached by Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev and West German Chancellor Helmut Kohl as regards the settlement of issues arising in view of German reunification and the long-term development of cooperation between the Soviet Union and united Germany on a broad basis. alternates.headline: Saddam Husayn succeeds al-Bakr as Iraq's president
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of July 17, 1979, listed under Iraq the ministerial appointments of Saddam Husayn's new government and, under Syria, an item that al-Asad had been informed in advance of al-Bakr's resignation.

alternates.headline: Ukraine declares state sovereignty
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of July 19, 1990, carried Kiev radio's text of the Declaration on the Ukraine's State Sovereignty adopted by the republic's Supreme Soviet on July 16, after a Moscow radio item on the session's continuing work.
